material.name: 4340 Steel
material.source: MakeItFrom, Annealed 4340 Ni-Cr-Mo Steel; density cross-checked against AZoM UNS G43400. Retrieved 2026-08-15.

ultimate_allowable.note: Tensile yield strength. UTS is 690 MPa.

fatigue_allowable.note: Published fatigue strength; the source does not state the cycle count.

hardness.note: The source's 220 HB, converted by ASTM E140. The flank allowable is ISO 6336-5:2016 Table 1's through-hardened alloy steel line at this hardness and the grade asked: 490 / 675 / 769 MPa at ML / MQ / ME.

material.name: 4340 Hardened Steel
material.condition: oil quenched from 845 °C, tempered at 425 °C — 46 HRC
material.source: ASM Desk Edition tempering table for oil-quenched 4340, as reproduced by theworldmaterial.com. Retrieved 2026-08-15.

ultimate_allowable.note: Tensile yield strength at this temper. UTS is 1500 MPa.

fatigue_allowable.note: 0.5 × UTS, the classical steel endurance ratio, which reproduces the annealed entry's published 330 MPa to within 5 %. No published fatigue figure was found at THIS temper. Treat as optimistic: the endurance ratio is known to fall away above roughly 1400 MPa UTS rather than track 0.5 indefinitely, so the true figure is plausibly nearer 700 MPa. The first number here worth replacing with your own data.

hardness.note: 46 HRC, the condition's, converted by ASTM E140. Past the end of ISO 6336-5:2016 Table 1's through-hardened alloy steel line (360 HV at ML and MQ, 390 at ME), where the table gives nothing, so the flank allowable is held at the line's end: 660.7 / 845.7 / 1123.1 MPa at ML / MQ / ME.
